name: City Council Regular Meeting of March 2, 2021
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF MARCH 2, 2021

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Pro Tem Martinez Muela
  s) Mayor Ancona  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.10.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

approximately 6:03 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

5.  INVOCATION:  Mayor Ancona.

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Chief of Police, David Reynoso. Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS: None

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Peggy Macias – Thank you again for the opportunity to speak with you again about the
impact Hero Pay would have on my co-workers and I. We have been out in the stores for
this whole pandemic not knowing whether we would be infected. When it first hit, there
wasn't a whole lot of good information on how to keep safe. Despite this, my co-workers
and I still went to work, day in and day out. Some were infected and others were lucky
enough not to get the COVID. I saw my co-workers come together as one and fight the
"COVID fight'. Along with health care workers, we knew the public needed our help. In
order to stay home, they needed food, toilet paper, cleaning supplies, etc.... And we
were there for them. That is why this Hero Pay is so important to us. Along with the
health care workers, we are true "Heroes". We ask you to support and pass an urgency
ordinance for Hero Pay. Thank you again for your time. Be safe!!!

Terrance Bacon – I am a pharmacy technician. I've been working in el monte for 10
years I truly believe hero pay for us would be amazing. We all have worked very during
these pandemic times with no rewards for putting our lives on the line. These companies
have not missed a beat because of the workers. In fact they have made major profits
over the time. I think it’s only fair to share it with the workers who drive the businesses.
We are counting on the city to do what’s right! Fight for the workers. Please pass hero
pay. We all deserve it for the continuous hard work we do! We ask you to support the
workers of this community and pass the ordinance for hero! Thanks you for your time!

Scoobaduck – In 2017, Councilmember Morales, then Planning Commissioner,
proposed a project for her property that was not allowed by the Municipal Code which is
the guiding document that puts regulations on what the City’s residents can and cannot
do on their property. In 2018, the Municipal Code was changed in a way that would allow
the Councilmember to propose and construct the project. I do not know if the change to
the Code was directly at the behest of the councilmember or simply a side conversation
with staff. However, I know that this change occurred when other residents must abide
by the Code as it is written without relying on changes. This is a betrayal of power by an
elected official who is meant to serve the community and be held to the same standards,
if not higher. I know that other elected officials have done this in the past, but it does not
make it right. I believe that the Councilmember has sown a seed that can fully bloom into
full-fledged corruption.

Andrea Diaz – I’m a CVS employee. I believe all essential workers deserve those 4$
years extra pay!!! We have all gone through so much since covid started. Some of us
even caught covid from sick customers. Personally I’ve had a really hard time, not only
with rude stressed out customers at work but at home to. My mother and father in law
ended up losing their jobs due to covid. It’s been really difficult for me and my boyfriend
to make ends meet these past few months and I believe if I were to get those 4$ extra
pay it’d help greatly. Thank you for taking your time to read my short experience.

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

Evangelica Child - I am a Health Policy Liaison with Day One here in El Monte at the Jeff
Seymour Center. My updates on Project Sticker Shock are that we have two interns who
are willing to make a change in the city. We have been reaching out to retail liquor stores
all across El Monte and there are currently 75 registered retailers who sell alcohol in El
Monte. We wish to continue to bring awareness to this issue and educate our youth of El
Monte on the harms of underage drinking. I would also like to highlight a few such as
Joy’s Market Place, Carltons Market, Tyler's Market and Los Toros Market that let us
place stickers on to multi packs of alcohol in their stores and were willing to partner with
us to spread the information about the cause. Thank you for your time.

Angelique Lopez – I am an intern for Day Ones’ Project Sticker Shock here in El Monte.
Project Sticker Shock is a collaborative awareness project with local retailers and
community members to spread awareness and education in order to dissuade adults
from purchasing alcohol on the behalf of minors and reduce underage drinking. The
warning stickers placed on multi-packs of beer or liquor is a positive way for the youth to
take responsibility and hold adults accountable from not selling to or purchasing for
minors.

Richie – I am a CVS employee for the City of El Monte and I would like you to consider
hazard pay for me and all my fellow employees I along with my colleagues have been in
the mix of this pandemic since the beginning , on a daily basis we deal with the public
we have COVID testing at our store and now will be offering the vaccine we deal with
sick customers coming in our store every day and we want and deserve to have hazards
pay given to us for the jobs we do.

Gabriel Zapata – I’m reaching out in regards to the hero pay. As a former citizen of El
Monte and still an essential in the city of El Monte I would greatly appreciate the hero
pay for the next 120 days. There are people who are getting their income through
unemployment and getting almost $2k for doing nothing. Why am I risking my life just to
get the same pay and barley making it? My hours are not consistent. My days are
always different every week. I’m never guaranteed the same amount of pay. It’s
extremely stressful. That’s why I would greatly appreciate this hero pay. Even if it’s just
for 120 days that is enough to help me pay my bills and provide for my family stress free.

Aaron Morfin – I am a pharmacy technician who works in the city of El Monte. I strongly
encourage hero pay is provided to us after our hard work and risking our lives working
day in and day out, providing vaccines, covid tests and continuous customer service to
all customers. All these efforts with no incentives or extra pay has taken a toll on us both
physically and mentally. Companies have received major profits and it is only fair tge
employees are rewarded for our efforts.

Alex Fulgencio – As an employee of CVS at store #9639 in El Monte I strongly push for
the county to go forward with the Hero Pay Act. We go through a lot dealing with
customer that come in sick not sure if it because of the flu or Covid we take big risks
every day we work not to mention all the rude customers that come in and don’t want to
wear a mask even though it’s still man dated. I urge you to please pass the Hero Pay Act
in El Monte is will help us out in the long run.

Anonymous – I wanted to express my extreme disappointment over something that was
brought to my attention and to several members of the community. A trusted member of
the community, witnessed Councilwoman Maria Morales receiving her COVID-19
vaccination 2 weeks ago at the Greater El Monte hospital. It is well known that up until

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

yesterday, vaccines were only being given to our most vulnerable populations,
specifically those 65 and older. The fact that Councilwoman Morales decided to JUMP
THE LINE, well in advance of LA County allowing educators to receive vaccines, brings
to light that this is an obvious abuse of power as an elected official. Let this be a
reminder that she was elected to serve the community, NOT HERSELF! Maria Morales
put her selfish needs, before that of our most vulnerable residents, OUR SENIORS!
Shame on Maria! And to add insult to injury, she was driven to the Greater El Monte
Hospital by TWO on duty police officers in an unmarked police vehicle. Upon her arrival,
she waited in the vehicle for the officers to open the door for her to exit her overpriced
chariot, funded by El Monte TAX PAYERS! The officers waited by her side until she
received her vaccine and then was released to go home. The TWO OFFICERS then,
opened the police car door for her as if they were her private chauffeurs and escorted
her home! Is this what we pay our officers to do? To be highly paid chauffeurs for the
power-hungry Undistinguished "Dr. Maria Morales". You would think with her high level
of education, she would have more common sense than to waste our highly needed tax
dollars. I thought police officers were paid to protect and serve our city? SHAME ON
MARIA MORALES for abusing her power to jump the line to get her vaccine and waste
the time of our police officers... and SHAME on City Manager Alma Martinez and Chief
of Police David Reynoso for allowing this abuse of power, giving special privileges and
wasting tax payer dollars. Maria Morales, you should be ashamed of yourself for being
vaccinated before thousands of Seniors in need. You are obviously serving your best
interest and not that of the community. What a disgrace!

Jazmin Palacios – I am a Pharmacy Technician working in the city of El Monte. I believe
that my hero pay should be passed there are so many hard working Essential workers.
Working endless hours trying to live through what looks like an endless pandemic. With
my hero pay passing, that would make a huge difference to everyone who has worked to
help all these companies thrive and make so much. I believe it’s time for us essential
workers to get some type of compensation for risking our health and helping so many
people.

Claudia Herrera – I been working for CVS for 11 yrs. Hero pay is important to me and
fair I expose myself every day, 40 sometimes 45 hours a week from covid, from people
that don’t ware mask, from people that walk in trying to get tested, from homeless that
walk in the store daily. I like my job I like the people I work with and is sad to know that
nobody take us serious, us essential workers never stop working since the pandemic
started we deserve a recomposition for all that hard work we have done. If it wasn’t for
us, people won’t have their essentials at home. Please vote yes on Hero Pay! Thank
you.

Zaira Arredondo – I work at cvs pharmacy. My current position is supervisor/ RX. I just
wanted to say that I am great full for my job but do believe we are put at risk greatly
every day. We are one of the busiest stores since the beginning of the pandemic till now.
Another fact is that we have a lot of people exposed to covid that either come in for
medication or are looking to get tested. We would really appreciate if we got offered the
hero pay.

Ryan Allain – On behalf of the California Retailers Association (CRA), inclusive of our
grocery and retail pharmacy members, we respectfully urge the Council to refrain from
passing a mandated a wage increase, especially in the absence of a complete economic
impact analysis on the effects such a mandate would have on essential businesses, and
subsequently, our local communities. The California Retailers Association is the only

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

statewide trade association representing all segments of the retail industry including
general merchandise, department stores, mass merchandisers, fast food restaurants,
convenience stores, supermarkets and grocery stores, chain drug, and specialty retail
such as auto, vision, jewelry, hardware and home stores. CRA works on behalf of
California’s retail industry, which currently operates over 164,200 stores and employs
around 2,776,000 people—nearly one fifth of California’s total employment. A mandated
pay increase beyond what retail employers can tolerate without raising prices or cutting
workforce hours will hurt both consumers and our hardworking employees. This is the
last thing our members want to do in the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic and
economic crisis. A number of our members are already offering substantial increases in
hourly pay and employee bonuses in recognition of the essential work these employees
are providing. An inflexible, one-size-fits-all approach risks increasing the cost of food,
grocery, and retail pharmacy drugs and will disproportionately impact those in our
communities who are already bearing the brunt of this pandemic. All of this comes on
top of the recent minimum wage increase. This is why we would request an economic
study before the Council mandates a substantial pay increase. We request that this
motion be amended to include an economic study prior to any consideration of an
increase in pay.

Allan Catanyag – We the frontliner in our way need your help to pass a bill that will
benefit our grocery workers in this Covid-19 pandemic as we served the people of El
Monte at this time. We all know how hard this days for each and everybody, most of us
coping that happened to us and we know how hard this now that we experienced the
sickness and even loss of our love one of this pandemic. May we have your helping
hand by approving this bill that in your table right now for the benefit of our hundreds of
our grocery workers that having problems in their finances. Thank you and the ball is in
your hands.

Jose Morfin – I believe we all deserve hero pay for what we’ve been doing and continue
to do. Constantly putting our lives at risk and getting no reward is not fair. We do more to
help people in these difficult times, but some disregard the pandemic and make our jobs
riskier. I’m hoping this Hero Pay would be the beginning of better things for all workers
who put their lives at risk.

Jennifer Lopez – I think it would be wonderful if you guys were to pass the hazard pay.
It would be great for employees.

Vanessa Rodriguez – I reside in the City of El Monte I work in CVS pharmacy located in
South El Monte I been working in pharmacy for almost 6 years now and I’ve seen first-
hand the impact that covid-19 has had in our community we’ve been working hard for
our patients to stay on their medications working sometimes 12 hours shifts to keep up
with the high demand of prescription we are the preferred pharmacy from Greater El
Monte hospital, helping patients positive for covid-19 I just would like emphasize how
important it is to keep our community in a healthy path to recovery from this pandemic.
Please help us too to continue working for our community with a rewarding pay.

Carlos Reyes – Been working at the market before covid. I'd admire the temporary hero
bonus wage but not at the cost of other stores closing down due to it. Still it doesn't
seem fair how we take the toll while the rest were being paid more to stay at home.

Antonio Franco – Hello I’ve been working as a pharmacy technician for almost three
years during the covid outbreak we had a lot of people who were sick and needed their

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

meds and might have had covid. We were essential without us working and giving
people their medications a lot of people would have gotten more sick. Our company
made billions in profits and would not increase our pay we deserve that pay. We need to
hold them responsible and we aren’t the only ones working during those times a lot of
grocery employees got covid because they had to work to provide for their family. During
this difficult time it has been hard to keep myself off debt my mom lost her job and I need
this hero pay to support my family. Please pass hero pay not just for our families but for
everyone working. We as a city are asking you to pass this bill most of us live in the
poverty level please help support those who need it.

Gabriel Ramirez – Just real quick I noticed that our Channel 3 local cable has been
restored because we were having problems hearing the audio via the computer the past
City Council meetings have been interrupted. I called Spectrum and Spectrum spoke to
the City so hopefully we can get that resolved because I am pretty sure we pay a lot of
money for the sound and in order for it to go on and off is unacceptable. Now going to
the point I noticed at the last City Council there was an anonymous person going after
Irma Zamorano in regards to the filing fees and I have heard a lot of rumors about myself
not paying the filing fee that it is coming from the City Clerk’s Office. My understanding
is that it is very breachment of information that a City Clerk or anyone at City Hall would
disclose of the status of the filing fee on the waiver to run for public office in November.
Myself and Irma are very concerned and I urge that the City Attorney to make an
investigation to see who had access to the files because now it is very concerning not
just to myself but for those who want to run for office who are being targeted by the
previous regime. I am very concerned about this that this happened ever. It never
happened until now. I am really concerned and I urge that the City Council and staff can
really look into this and have an independent investigation.

Alexis Proctor – I was wondering if the City can adopt a program with support of the
County that if a person gets written up for a violation by the County or the City in general
that we adopt a program where a person be able to fill an application qualifying for low
income and given like a fee waiver. [INAUDIBLE]

Robert Morgof – [INAUDIBLE]

Mark Ramos – I would like to urge my support for the item and I urge the Council to
direct staff to draft an ordinance to support grocery workers and retail workers in town.
Other cities nearby have done the same last night Pomona. The grocers and retailers
have made record profits in this past year although we heard earlier from retail
association describe a hardship we have not seen that but it comes to the owners and
the executives of these corporations whether it is Walgreens or Kroeger by giving multi-
million dollar stock buy backs to rich stock holders and executives while leaving the
workers on the frontline to fight the battle. We think it is time for these workers to be
shown some respect for their efforts for their sacrifice. These members show up every
day to do their jobs to make sure that folks have food on their tables to have what their
need. Our members have done their jobs they make sure they report to work every day
risking infection as you heard other and financial hardship and receiving nothing from
their companies.

Damian Martin – I am speaking on Item 4.5 from Closed Session. My client submitted a
settlement offer to the City and the purpose of this comment is just to provide some
context. In addition to being Legal Counsel I also put together multiple applications that
were successful for cannabis retailers in the City of El Monte. I know the application

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

  backwards and forwards they are my babies they really are I am super passionate about
  this because of that I was able to quickly identify an error by the City’s consultant that
  came in to score the premises diagram. Nibble This submitted a diagram exactly as one
  of the winning applicant ye the winning applicant received a perfect score and Nibble
  This my client did not they received a point deduction. Have they received that additional
  point Nibble This would have been the sixth point applicant and winning the license. So
  there is a clear mistake with what the consultant that was hired had done. The purpose
  of the settlement offer is not to create a liability or a bunch of embarrassment mistakes
  happen it is a natural part in this complex process and so the settlement offer is just to
  kind of move forward and move past it. The ordinance itself includes a mechanism for
  addressing mistakes essentially the City Council under the right circumstances has the
  right to issue additional licenses and really that is all my client is looking for at this point
  is to have the City Council issue it a license. My client doesn’t want to take a license
  from anyone else we don’t think it is productive for the City to trade one lawsuit for
  another and ultimately the goal is to move forward. My client established itself in the
  application as a very strong applicant with really strong community benefits with a high
  likelihood of successful operation that is all my client wants to do at this point. They want
  to get their license, they want to open a successful business in the City of El Monte they
  want to put money in the City of El Monte and generate tremendous community benefits.

9.  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT: None

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda.
  One or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be
  discussed, considered and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded
  motion of any member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council
  quorum.

  10
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 2, 2021

12.1  Waiver of Full Reading of Ordinance(s).

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Approval to waive full reading (except title) of all ordinances appearing on the
